blocks.title: What the work is like.
rows: From day ten you are in their standup, on their repo and their board. We manage you; they direct the work. You are never the junior in the room.
No context-switching between three clients. When an engagement ends there is a planned gap, not a bench.
Every build runs on our Claude Code pipeline: you plan with an agent, review what it writes, and decide. You will write less boilerplate and more judgement.
Every change is reviewed by a second senior before it lands, yours included. That is the quality bar, not a hierarchy.
The overlap with GMT is 09:00 to 13:00 Lahore time, the same four hours every day. Afternoons are deep work, not meetings.

blocks.title: How we vet.
blocks.sub: Five steps, two weeks, no whiteboard puzzles.
rows: Send us something you shipped and owned in production: what it did, what broke, what you would do differently.
An hour on that system with one of us. We go deep on one thing rather than wide on everything.
A real problem from a real engagement, paid at the day rate, with the pipeline. We look at the judgement, not the speed.
Two people who have shipped with you. We call them.
Written, with the band, the overlap and the first engagement if there is one lined up.

blocks.title: Roles we hire for.
rows: .NET, Node.js or Python; owned a production system; comfortable in someone else's codebase
React or Angular, with the design-system discipline to keep three brands one product
Pipelines that run without you; warehouse, semantic layer, dashboards people open
Retrieval, evaluation harnesses, agents on Claude Code and MCP; a number before a demo
Kotlin, AOSP or cross-platform; store-ready, offline-first where it matters
Pay: [PAY BANDS BY LEVEL] · paid monthly in [PKR / USD] · equipment provided · [LEAVE POLICY]

items.q: Do I have to be in Lahore?
items.a: Remote within Pakistan is fine; the overlap hours are what matter. [OFFICE DAYS, IF ANY].
A planned gap: paid, with a date for the next start. We staff for engagements, so gaps are short and known in advance; we do not run a bench.

items.q: Will I be a contractor or an employee?
items.a: [EMPLOYMENT MODEL]. Written in the offer, with the band and the notice period.

items.q: Can I say no to a client?
items.a: Yes, before you start. You meet the client before day one, and so do they; either side can say no.
